summary: Hans Küng worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum (~1947–1954), the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1947–1955), and the Catholic University of Paris (~1955–1956), and held a post at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1996).
Hans Martin Krämer is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He studied at Ruhr University Bochum from ~1993 to 2000 and held a post there around 2008.

Hans T. Bakker is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink (~1974–1984). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1988–1996), the University of Groningen (~1996–2013), and the British Museum (curator, retired 2014).
Hans Urs von Balthasar was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Bernhard Geiger from 1924 to 1926 and at the University of Zurich from ~1927 to 1929.
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1935).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp (~1959–1963) and Gustav Mensching (~1965–1968), whom he succeeded in 1972 upon becoming Direktor at the University of Bonn.
Hans-Werbin Köhler is an Indologist who studied under teacher Eduard Hermann and completed his doctoral studies under supervisor Ernst Waldschmidt.
Hansa Dhammahaso is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as director at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and the International Buddhist Studies College, both attested in 2017.

Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Kim earned a Master's degree at Columbia University and a Ph.D. at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.
Har Dayal was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Delhi and subsequently at SOAS University of London from ~1927 to 1932.

Harald Hauptmann worked in archaeology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg, and FU Berlin, he held posts at the German Archaeological Institute, FU Berlin, Heidelberg University, the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Istanbul.

Haraprasad Shastri studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Presidency University, and Sanskrit College. A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Hare School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Presidency University, Sanskrit College, The Asiatic Society, and the University of Dhaka.

Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He held posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and served as Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).

Hari Shankar Prasad works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, under Ramakant Tripathi, and under doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong (attested 1982).

Haridas Bhattacharyya studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. An Indologist and philosopher, he held posts at Scottish Church College (1915), the University of Calcutta (1917), the University of Dhaka (1921), and Banaras Hindu University (1947).
Haridas Sinharay is an Indology scholar who held an academic post at Maulana Azad College, attested in both 1970 and 1990.

Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani studied at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and under Muni Jinavijaya. A scholar in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Gujarat University, and the L. D. Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University. Working in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology, he assumed a chair in Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia (~1987).
Harogadde Manappa Nayak was a scholar of linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1967–1984) and as Vice-chancellor at Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin studied at UC Berkeley (1943–1950) and Yale (Ph.D. ~1953–1955). Active in linguistics, he held posts at Columbia University (1955), Yale University (1962–1996), and as Curator of Anthropology at the Peabody Museum (1974–1996).
